newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN OLO MARKET FORGETS FRANCE, LOOKS TO U.S.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN OLO MARKET FORGETS FRANCE, LOOKS TO U.S.

text.p: This week's raft of U.S. data will make the Belgian linear bond (OLO) market forget its apprehension about French elections, dealers said on Monday.

Two polls -- one late Sunday and one on Monday -- showed the French centre-right government ahead of opposition left parties. The news gave no support to the Belgian market in contrast to a poll last Thursday showing only a narrow lead for the pro-EMU government, which had sent prices tumbling.
"The main problem for this week is that we have a lot of figures in the U.S., particularly towards the weekend, and that will put pressure on the market," one CERA bank trader said.
The benchmark 10-year OLO yield was steady at 6.04 percent early on Monday, but the Belgian market slightly underperformed Bunds. OLO futures were lower.
The front-month OLO contract was off 0.06 at 119.91 by 0730 GMT after edging slightly higher at the start.

"The upside potential remains limited. The uncertainty of the U.S. data is weighing on the market...but whether we are in a bear market remains to be seen. I personally don't see any reason for higher yields in Europe," the CERA bank trader added.
He said the market would not take a firm direction until after Friday's U.S. April employment report.
Before then players will have to digest U.S. new homes sales (1400 GMT), employment cost index and durable goods orders (Tuesday) and first quarter GDP (Wednesday.
The market is closed on Thursday for May Day, when U.S. data releases include the April national association of purchasing managers (NAPM) index and weekly jobless claims.
